definition_zh: 祈祷；祷告；恳求；央求；祈盼
definition_en: to speak to a god in worship or in request, and also to ask a person or fate for something with great earnestness
core_image: 一个人双手合在胸前，把心里的愿望说给看不见的听者
scene: 教堂里的灯很暗，老妇人在长椅前跪下，双手交握，嘴唇轻轻动着。 She knelt in the dim church and began to pray for her grandson's recovery.
sceneCN: 这里是「祈祷、祷告」（第 1 个义项：向神说话）；句意为她在昏暗的教堂里跪下，开始为孙子的康复祈祷。图中可辨识物件：长椅、昏暗的灯、交握的双手。

derivatives.zh: 由 pray 加 -er 构成的名词，指「祷告」或「祷文」；作「祈祷者」讲时读作 pray-er，与前者读音不同
prayer 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「虔诚祈祷的」
prayerful 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「虔诚地祈祷着」

senses.title: To speak to a god in prayer
senses.definition: to address a god or a higher power, usually in words, in order to worship, give thanks or ask for help
senses.definitionCN: 向神或某种更高力量说话，通常用言语，以表达敬拜、感恩或求助
senses.example: The villagers pray in the small chapel every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们每天早晨都在小教堂里祈祷。
senses.why: The Latin verb precari meant to beg or entreat, so the oldest English use of pray is exactly this: turning a request toward someone believed to be able to answer it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 precari 本义是「恳求、央求」，pray 最早的意思正是如此：把请求说给一个被认为有能力回应的人听。

senses.title: To ask someone earnestly
senses.definition: to ask a person for something in a humble and urgent way, as though begging
senses.definitionCN: 以谦卑而急切的语气向某人提出请求，近乎哀求
senses.example: I pray you, do not tell him what I said.
senses.exampleCN: 我求您了，别把我说的告诉他。
senses.why: Because the word began as an act of begging, it could be aimed at a person as easily as at a god; this everyday sense still survives in set phrases such as pray tell.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本来就表示「乞求」，所以既可以对着神说，也可以对着人说；这一日常义项仍保留在 pray tell 这类固定说法里。

senses.title: To hope for something very strongly
senses.definition: to want something to happen very much, often expressed as a wish rather than a request to any particular listener
senses.definitionCN: 非常希望某事发生，往往只是表达愿望，并不真的说给某个特定听者
senses.example: We pray that the rains come before the wells run dry.
senses.exampleCN: 我们祈盼在井水干涸之前下雨。
senses.why: Once praying is framed as a request for an outcome, the outcome itself can fill the whole meaning, so the verb slides from talking to a god into simply hoping hard.
senses.whyCN: 当祈祷被理解成「为某个结果提出请求」，结果本身就占满了整个词义，于是动词从「对神说话」滑向「强烈地盼望」。

senses.title: Please, in old-fashioned polite formulas
senses.definition: used in older or formal English to soften a request, roughly meaning please
senses.definitionCN: 在较古旧或正式的英语中用来缓和请求，大致相当于「请」
senses.example: Pray be seated; the doctor will see you shortly.
senses.exampleCN: 请坐，医生很快就给您看诊。
senses.why: The begging sense weakened into pure politeness, so the verb became a formula for softening a request, much as please did.
senses.whyCN: 「乞求」的语气逐渐弱化成纯粹的礼貌，动词便成了缓和请求的套语，作用和 please 相近。

senses.title: To offer worship in words
senses.definition: to worship a god by speaking, whether aloud or in silence
senses.definitionCN: 以言语敬拜神，可出声亦可默念
senses.example: They prayed together before the journey began.
senses.exampleCN: 动身之前他们一起做了祷告。
senses.why: Worship is the respectful side of addressing a god, beside the asking side.
senses.whyCN: 敬拜是对神说话的另一面，与祈求并行。

senses.title: To ask as a favour from God
senses.definition: to ask God to grant something wanted or needed
senses.definitionCN: 求神赐予所愿望或所需要的东西
senses.example: The farmers prayed for rain all through the dry month.
senses.exampleCN: 整个干旱的月份里，农民一直在求雨。
senses.why: Begging turned upward needs only an object: what is begged for becomes the whole content of the prayer.
senses.whyCN: 向上仰求的乞求只需一个对象：所求之物就成了祷告的全部内容。

senses.title: To hope very hard for a result
senses.definition: to wish for an outcome with great intensity, often without formal religious intent
senses.definitionCN: 极其强烈地盼望某个结果，常不带正式的宗教意图
senses.example: I am praying that the roads stay clear tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我巴望着今晚路别封上。
senses.why: The request shrinks to a wish: once the hearer is optional, only the longing remains.
senses.whyCN: 请求收缩为愿望：听者既可有可无，剩下的就只有那份盼望。

senses.title: To pray in aid or in aid of: to invoke help
senses.definition: in old legal use, to call upon someone or something for assistance
senses.definitionCN: 旧法律用语中，指祈求某人或某物给予援助
senses.example: The medieval defendant prayed in aid of his neighbours' testimony.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的被告祈求邻居出庭作证。
senses.why: Begging kept its legal shape long after the courtroom borrowed it, so the old verb survives in formulas.
senses.whyCN: 乞求被法庭借用后长期保留其法律形态，古旧的动词便留存在套语里。

intro.en: Pray comes from a Latin verb of begging; the religious sense is a specialised use of that older, everyday act of asking.
intro.cn: pray 来自拉丁语中表示「乞求」的动词；宗教上的「祈祷」只是这个更古老、更日常的「求人」动作的专门用法。

items.en: A root usually reconstructed as *prek-, meaning to ask or request, is thought to lie behind the Latin verb; the form is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁动词背后有一个常被重构为 *prek- 的词根，意为「请求、询问」；这是重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Precari meant to entreat, beg or ask, and its noun prex, with the stem prec-, named a prayer or a request.
items.cn: precari 意为恳求、乞求、请求，其名词 prex（词干 prec-）指祈祷或请求。

items.en: Old French preier, later written prier, meant both to ask a person and to address God, and it is the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 preier（后来写作 prier）既指向人请求，也指向神说话，英语借的正是这个形式。

items.en: Middle English prayen carried the double sense of asking a person and praying to God, and the spelling settled as pray.
items.cn: 中古英语 prayen 同时保留「求人」和「求神」两义，拼写后来固定为 pray。

items.en: Modern English keeps the religious sense as the main one; the older begging sense survives in fixed phrases, and the derived noun prayer has developed a shortened pronunciation of its own.
items.cn: 现代英语以宗教义为主；较古的「恳求」义残留在固定短语中，派生名词 prayer 也发展出自己缩短的读音。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share letters or the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of asking or of addressing a higher power.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示「请求」或「向更高力量说话」的词。

entries.definition: An animal hunted by another animal for food; from Latin praeda.
entries.definitionCN: 猎物；被捕食的动物。只是读音与拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The noun built on pray, naming the act or the words of praying.
entries.definitionCN: 由 pray 派生的名词，指祈祷的行为或祷文。

entries.definition: To look too closely into something private, or to force something open.
entries.definitionCN: 窥探；撬开。只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To express disapproval of something; from Latin deprecari, literally to pray away.
entries.definitionCN: 反对；不赞成。源自拉丁语 deprecari，字面是「祈祷着把某事推开」。

entries.definition: To ask for something in an urgent or humble way.
entries.definitionCN: 急切或卑微地请求；乞求。

entries.definition: To ask for something in a serious and emotional way.
entries.definitionCN: 恳切地请求；恳求。

entries.definition: To ask someone urgently and sincerely for something.
entries.definitionCN: 恳切而真诚地请求；哀求。

entries.definition: To show deep respect and love for a god, especially in a service.
entries.definitionCN: 敬拜；礼拜，尤指在仪式中表达对神的敬爱与尊崇。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of begging, and its family shows how asking a person turned into addressing a god.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「乞求」的动词，它的同族词显示出「求人」如何转成「求神」。

normal.en: Precari in Latin means to beg; pray keeps that posture of asking rather than demanding.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 precari 意为乞求，pray 保留了「请求」而不是「要求」的姿态。

normal.en: Prec- is the stem of prex, a prayer or request, so the same stem carries the act of asking.
normal.cn: prec- 是 prex（祈祷、请求）的词干，同一个词干承载着「请求」这个动作。

normal.en: Pray for peace, pray for rain: the pattern pray for plus a thing names what you want to happen.
normal.cn: pray for peace、pray for rain：pray for 后面接一件事，就点明了希望发生什么。

normal.en: Pray tell is a fossil of the old sense: there pray means I beg you, not I worship.
normal.cn: pray tell 是旧义的化石：那里的 pray 意为「我求您」，而不是「我敬拜」。

normal.en: A praying mantis is named for its raised forelegs, which look like hands held in prayer.
normal.cn: praying mantis（螳螂）得名于它举起的前足，看上去像合十祈祷的手。

abstract.en: Praying is a wish given an address: the same words would be only a hope if no one were listening.
abstract.cn: 祈祷是给愿望写上了收件人：若没有听者，同样的话就只是希望。

abstract.en: Asking a person and asking a god use the same verb, which quietly admits how alike the two acts feel.
abstract.cn: 求人和求神用同一个动词，这等于默认两种动作在感觉上多么相似。

abstract.en: A prayer may leave the world unchanged, but it usually leaves the speaker rearranged.
abstract.cn: 祈祷未必改变世界，却往往把祈祷的人重新整理了一遍。

examples.en: She knelt by the bed and prayed for her son.
examples.cn: 她在床边跪下，为儿子祈祷。

examples.en: We pray that the bridge holds until help arrives.
examples.cn: 我们祈盼这座桥能撑到救援到来。

examples.en: Pray tell me what happened at the meeting.
examples.cn: 请告诉我会上发生了什么。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑雷」——急得心里扑通打雷，只好开口求人；pray 便是恳求、祈祷。

root: 拉丁语 precari（恳求、祈求），名词 prex（词干 prec-，祈祷、请求）；经古法语 preier 进入英语，同族词多与「请求」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a request sent upward; the senses divide by who is addressed, a god, a person, or no one in particular, and by how far the request has faded into politeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「向上发出的请求」；义项按说给谁听分出向神、向人、只对结果说话三等，也按请求语气的弱化分出客套用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with hands pressed together, sending a wish toward a listener who cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人双手合十，把愿望送给一个看不见的听者。

branches.en: a woman kneeling in a dim chapel, whispering a request
branches.cn: 昏暗小教堂里跪着低声祈求的女人

branches.en: a servant on one knee, begging his master for mercy
branches.cn: 单膝跪地、向主人求饶的仆人

branches.en: a farmer watching the sky, asking for rain that may not come
branches.cn: 农夫望着天，求一场也许不会来的雨

branches.en: a letter ending with one courtly please
branches.cn: 一封信末尾那句客气的「请」

branches.en: the same raised hands, once to a god and once to the weather
branches.cn: 同样举起的双手，一次朝着神，一次朝着天气

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of entreaty, its noun stem, an Old French reshaping, and English endings that mark the person and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中表示恳求的动词、它的名词词干、古法语的改写，以及标记「人」与「性质」的英语词尾共同构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the verb of entreaty and its noun stem, which English later reshaped through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示恳求的动词及其名词词干，英语又经法语对它做了改写。

items.meaning: to address a god; to beg

latinEntries.meaning: to pray against, to avert by prayer
latinEntries.meaningCN: 祈祷着把某事推开；祈求免除

definition_en: to break and move earth, or to search deeply for something
core_image: 铁锹插进湿土，翻起一铲发黑的泥，旁边堆起小小的土丘
scene: 院子里那棵老树旁，男人一铲一铲往下探。 They dug a narrow hole beside the fence.
sceneCN: 这里 dug 指「挖」（第 1 个义项：把土翻开）；句意是他们在篱笆旁挖了一个窄洞。

derivatives.zh: 挖掘者；挖掘机
挖掘；发掘

senses.title: To turn the earth
senses.definition: to break the ground and lift the soil away
senses.definitionCN: 把地面破开，把土铲走
senses.example: They dug a narrow hole beside the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在篱笆旁挖了一个窄洞。
senses.why: The hand works downward and the ground gives way.
senses.whyCN: 手往下使劲，地就让开了。

senses.title: To search deep below
senses.definition: to look for something by going far below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 钻到表层以下很远去找东西
senses.example: The team dug for old coins all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天，这支队伍都在挖找古币。
senses.why: What is wanted lies under a layer, and the layer must be removed.
senses.whyCN: 想要的东西在一层东西下面，那层必须被搬开。

senses.title: A small cutting remark
senses.definition: a short remark that quietly makes fun of someone
senses.definitionCN: 一句不动声色取笑别人的短话
senses.example: He took the dig about his old car quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 别人挖苦他那辆旧车，他没作声。
senses.why: A remark can go under the skin the way a spade goes under soil.
senses.whyCN: 一句话能钻进皮肉，像铲子钻进泥土。

intro.en: Dig appears in Middle English as diggen, probably from an Anglo-French verb for cutting a ditch.
intro.cn: dig 在中古英语里写作 diggen，可能出自表示「开沟」的英法混合语动词。

items.en: Digue meant a dike, a bank raised to hold water.
items.cn: digue 指堤坝，为挡水而筑起的土埂。

items.en: Diguer meant to cut a ditch or a channel.
items.cn: diguer 指开沟、挖渠。

items.en: Diggen took the plain sense of moving earth with a tool.
items.cn: diggen 承接了「用工具翻土」这层直白意思。

items.en: The verb widened to hunting for buried things.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到寻找埋在地下的东西。

items.en: Dig also became a noun for a teasing remark and for a site being explored.
items.cn: dig 还变成名词，指一句取笑的话或一处发掘地。

note.en: The look-alike group is close in spelling, while the meaning group covers digging, tunnelling and searching deep.
note.cn: 形近组拼写接近，近义组则覆盖挖掘、打洞与深入寻找。

entries.definition: a person or machine that digs
entries.definitionCN: 挖掘的人或机器

entries.definition: a long wall of earth built to hold water back
entries.definitionCN: 为挡水而筑的长土堤

entries.definition: the past form of dig
entries.definitionCN: dig 的过去式

entries.definition: to remove earth carefully from a site
entries.definitionCN: 在现场小心地挖走泥土

entries.definition: to make a hole or tunnel and live in it
entries.definitionCN: 打洞或钻隧道并住在里面

entries.definition: to search deeply into a subject or a container
entries.definitionCN: 深入探究某个题目或翻找容器

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a spade biting wet soil and end with a remark that bites a person.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从铁锹咬进湿土开始，最后落到一句咬人的话。

normal.en: Dig, dug, dug: the vowel drops as the spade goes down.
normal.cn: dig、dug、dug：铲子往下走，元音也跟着沉下去。

normal.en: Dig up brings to the surface; dig into goes further in.
normal.cn: dig up 是把东西翻上来，dig into 是继续往里走。

normal.en: Dig deep is advice for muscles and for courage.
normal.cn: dig deep 既是对肌肉说的，也是对勇气说的。

normal.en: An archaeologist digs slowly because the past breaks easily.
normal.cn: 考古的人挖得慢，因为过去一碰就碎。

normal.en: A dig in conversation leaves no hole, only a bruise.
normal.cn: 话里的 dig 不留洞，只留一块淤青。

abstract.en: Picture a spade cutting a clean line in dark soil.
abstract.cn: 想象铁锹在黑土上切出一道干净的线。

abstract.en: Picture a small hill of earth growing beside a hole.
abstract.cn: 想象洞旁边慢慢堆起一座小土丘。

abstract.en: Picture a hand brushing dust off something buried.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手拂去埋着的东西上的土。

examples.en: The dog dug under the gate again.
examples.cn: 那条狗又在门底下刨洞了。

examples.en: She dug into the old records for hours.
examples.cn: 她在旧档案里翻找了好几个小时。

examples.en: He made a quiet dig about her lateness.
examples.cn: 他轻声挖苦了一句她迟到的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dig 记成「地哥」：地哥拿着铲子，一寸寸往地里探。

root: 中古英语作 diggen，可能来自表示「开沟」的英法混合语 diguer，而 digue 指堤坝。本义是用工具翻土开沟，后来扩展到挖掘寻找埋藏之物，也用于比喻深入探究；作名词时，又指一句带刺的取笑话或一处发掘现场。

sensesIntro.en: From a spade lifting soil, to a search under the surface, to a remark that goes under the skin.
sensesIntro.cn: 从铁锹翻土，到地表之下的寻找，再到一句钻进皮肉的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spade biting into wet soil and lifting it aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁锹咬进湿土，再把它掀到一边。

chain: A WORD CUTS UNDER THE SKIN

branches.en: The first sense is the plain act of moving earth.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是翻土这个直白动作。

branches.en: The second sense adds a purpose and a depth.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了目的与深度。

branches.en: The third sense turns the tool into a remark.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把工具换成了一句话。

branches.en: Every excavation begins with one shovel of soil.
branches.cn: 每一次发掘都从一铲土开始。

branches.en: Both go below the surface, one for facts and one for feeling.
branches.cn: 两者都往表层以下走，一个找事实，一个碰感受。

intro.en: Dig forms a small family of tools, actions and holes, with almost no Latin help.
intro.cn: dig 长出一小族词，涉及工具、动作与洞穴，几乎不靠拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and French in origin; there is no Latin base behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根出自日耳曼语与法语，这一族词背后没有拉丁词基。

items.example: They dig a well every spring.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年春天挖一口井。

items.example: The digger cleared the whole bank.
items.exampleCN: 挖掘机清空了整道土坡。

items.example: Digging here is slow and careful.
They dug the trench by hand.
He digs the garden every autumn.

items.meaning: a hole in the ground used as shelter
items.example: The soldiers waited in a dugout.

items.meaning: earth removed, or a place being worked
items.example: The old diggings are now a park.
items.exampleCN: 那片旧采掘场如今是个公园。

definition_en: the real facts about a situation, or a principle that is generally accepted as correct
core_image: 一束光照进昏暗的房间，灰尘和每件东西都被照得清清楚楚
scene: 孩子问起一件旧事，屋里安静下来，大人终于开口。 In the end the truth about the broken window came out.
sceneCN: 这里 truth 是「真相；实情」（第 1 个义项：关于某个情况的真实事实）；句意为打破窗子的真相最后终于水落石出。光把昏室里每件东西照亮，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: truth 的词根形容词，义为「真实的」
由 truth 加 -ful 构成，义为「诚实的）
由 un-（否定）与 truth 复合，义为「假话；不实」

senses.title: What really happened
senses.definition: the real facts of a situation, as opposed to what people say or believe
senses.definitionCN: 某种情况的真实事实，与人们的说法或相信的内容相对
senses.example: In the end the truth about the broken window came out.
senses.exampleCN: 打破窗子的真相最后终于水落石出。
senses.why: The noun is built on true with the old ending -th, so truth is literally the state of being true.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词以 true 加古老词尾 -th 构成，truth 字面上就是「真实的状态」。

senses.title: A principle that holds
senses.definition: a belief or rule that is accepted by many as always correct
senses.definitionCN: 被许多人认为始终正确的信念或法则
senses.example: The book is a search for simple truths about human life.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是对人类生活中几条朴素真理的探寻。
senses.why: A statement true in all cases becomes an idea of truth: a principle that never fails.
senses.whyCN: 在所有情况下都成立的陈述，就成了「真理」这一观念的载体：一条从不失效的法则。

senses.title: The quality of being true
senses.definition: the fact of being accurate or genuine
senses.definitionCN: 准确或真挚的事实
senses.example: There is some truth in what he says.
senses.exampleCN: 他说的有几分道理。
senses.why: Here the word names a measured amount of accuracy, as in there is some truth in it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指可度量的准确程度，如「其中有一点真实的成分」那样。

intro.en: Truth was formed in Old English from treowe, faithful, by adding the suffix -th, the same ending as in width.
intro.cn: truth 在古英语中由 treowe（忠信）加后缀 -th 构成，与 width 里的词尾相同。

items.en: A very old root meaning firm and trustworthy lies behind the Germanic word for loyal, and it survives in the family of true and truth.
items.cn: 一个意为牢固、可信赖的极古老词根藏在日耳曼语表示忠实的词后面，并在 true 与 truth 的词族里留存下来。

items.en: The root treuwaz meant firm and loyal, shared by true and truth.
items.cn: 词根 treuwaz 意为牢固、忠实，由 true 与 truth 共享。

items.en: Treowth meant faithfulness, a promise kept between people.
items.cn: treowth 意为忠信，人与人之间守住的承诺。

items.en: Middle English truth moved from faithfulness toward agreement with facts.
items.cn: 中古英语 truth 从忠信转向与事实相符。

items.en: The sense of a general principle settled in the early modern period.
items.cn: 「普遍原理」的意义在近代早期固定下来。

items.en: In truth and to tell the truth keep the everyday spoken force of the word.
items.cn: in truth 与 to tell the truth 保留了这个词的日常口语力量。

note.en: The first group shares the tru stem, the second holds other words for facts and accuracy.
note.cn: 第一组共享 tru 词干，第二组收其他表示事实与准确的词。

entries.definition: Agreeing with the facts.
entries.definitionCN: 真实的

entries.definition: Telling the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 诚实的

entries.definition: Really and sincerely.
entries.definitionCN: 真正地

entries.definition: Something known to have happened.
entries.definitionCN: 事实

entries.definition: The way things really are.
entries.definitionCN: 现实

entries.definition: Correctness in detail.
entries.definitionCN: 准确性

normalIntro.en: Truth is true with a -th ending, much like warm becomes warmth.
normalIntro.cn: truth 就是 true 加上 -th 词尾，很像 warm 变成 warmth。

normal.en: The -th ending turns an adjective into a noun of state.
normal.cn: -th 词尾把形容词变成状态名词。

normal.en: The plural changes nothing but adds s: truths.
normal.cn: 复数不变形，只加 s：truths。

normal.en: Tell the truth is the simplest phrase built on it.
normal.cn: tell the truth 是它最简单的搭配。

normal.en: The vowel is long, as in food.
normal.cn: 元音是长音，像 food。

normal.en: In truth sits at the start of a sentence like a signal.
normal.cn: in truth 像信号一样放在句首。

abstract.en: Light falling into a dusty room and showing everything.
abstract.cn: 光照进积尘的房间，把一切都显出来。

abstract.en: A door finally opened on the room that was there all along.
abstract.cn: 一扇门终于打开，露出一直都在的房间。

abstract.en: A heavy object set down after being carried a long way.
abstract.cn: 一个被扛了很远的重物终于放下。

examples.en: He told the truth even though it cost him his job.
examples.cn: 他说出了真相，尽管因此丢了工作。

examples.en: There is a little truth in every old story.
examples.cn: 每个古老故事里都有一点真实。

examples.en: Scientists look for truths that hold in every case.
examples.cn: 科学家寻找在任何情况下都成立的真理。

dict_mnemonic.text: true＋th——像宽是 width、暖是 warmth，真是 truth：真实的状态就是真相。

root: 古英语 treowth，由 treowe（忠信）加 -th 构成，与日耳曼语词根 treuwaz（牢固、忠实）同源；同族词有 true、truthful、untruth。

sensesIntro.en: First the facts of a case, then a principle that always holds, then the amount of accuracy a claim contains.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是案情的实情，再是始终成立的原理，最后是一句话所含的准确程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light entering a dusty room.
core.cn: 核心意象：照进积尘房间的光。

branches.en: The fact branch: what really happened.
branches.cn: 事实分支：真正发生的事。

branches.en: The principle branch: a rule that never fails.
branches.cn: 原理分支：从不失效的法则。

branches.en: The degree branch: some truth in a claim.
branches.cn: 程度分支：一句话里有几分真。

branches.en: The honesty branch: both rest on a word kept.
branches.cn: 诚实分支：两者都建立在守住的话上。

branches.en: The evidence branch: measuring how much holds.
branches.cn: 证据分支：衡量有多少站得住。

intro.en: Truth is the stem tru plus the old noun ending -th, which English still uses in a few words.
intro.cn: truth 是词干 tru 加古老名词词尾 -th，英语至今只在少数词里用它。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below express truth and faith from another family.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词出自另一词族，表达真实与信义。

items.example: The stem is the adjective with the e dropped.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干是去掉 e 的形容词。

items.example: It forms truth, the state of being true.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 truth，真实的状态。

items.example: It forms truthful, full of truth.
It forms untruth, a false statement.
The adjective keeps its final e.
Truths of every age were compared.
items.exampleCN: 各个时代的真理被放在一起比较。
这个形容词描述说话的人。

definition_zh: 财产；所有物；房产；不动产；性质；特性
definition_en: something owned, especially land or buildings, or a quality that belongs to a thing
core_image: 一块地界石立在草地边缘，石面刻着主人的记号，旁边摆着屋内可搬动的器物
scene: 遗产清册上，房子、田地与家具都列在同一栏，标明归谁所有。 The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
sceneCN: 这里指「归某人所有的财物与地产」，对应第 1 个义项：被拥有、可被继承的物；句意为清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏并注明归属。画面要点：地界石、主人的记号、并列的器物；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 财产；所有物；房产（不可数，指财物总体；表示一件件具体物品时可用复数）
性质；特性（可数，常用于科学语境，指某物固有的属性）

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

senses.title: Things that belong to someone
senses.definition: the things a person owns, taken as a whole, including goods, money and rights
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所拥有的东西的总和，包括货物、金钱与权利
senses.example: The estate inventory listed the house, the land and the furniture in one column, each item marked as property belonging to a named heir.
senses.exampleCN: 遗产清册把房子、田地和家具列在同一栏，每件都注明属于某位继承人的财产。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'one's own', so the word begins as a label for whatever answers the question 'whose is it'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为「自己的」，因此这个词起初就是给「这是谁的」这一问题的答案贴标签。

senses.title: Land and buildings
senses.definition: real estate, especially a house or plot that can be bought, sold or rented
senses.definitionCN: 不动产，尤指可买卖或出租的房屋或地块
senses.example: Property prices rose along the new railway.
senses.exampleCN: 新铁路沿线的房价上涨了。
senses.why: Land is the one thing that cannot be carried away, so it became the clearest test of who owns what.
senses.whyCN: 土地是唯一搬不走的东西，因此它成为「谁拥有什么」最清楚的检验。

senses.title: The right of ownership itself
senses.definition: the legal power to use, exclude others from, sell or give away a thing
senses.definitionCN: 使用某物、排除他人、出售或赠予该物的法律权力
senses.example: Property is a bundle of rights, not merely the object held.
senses.exampleCN: 所有权是一束权利，而不只是手中所持之物。
senses.why: Lawyers separate the object from the right over it, and the word covers both, which is why one can own property in property.
senses.whyCN: 法学家把物与对物的权利分开，而这个词同时覆盖两者，所以人可以对财产享有财产权。

senses.title: A quality belonging to a thing
senses.definition: a characteristic that a substance or object has, such as colour, hardness or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或物体所具有的特征，如颜色、硬度或导电性
senses.example: The property that makes the alloy useful is its resistance to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 使这种合金有用的性质是它的耐热性。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing in the oldest sense includes not only goods but traits, because a trait is also something 'its own'.
senses.whyCN: 最古老意义上的「属于」不只包括财物，也包括特征，因为特征同样是某物「自己的」东西。

senses.title: Property in intangible things
senses.definition: ownership of ideas, marks, designs or other intangibles protected by law
senses.definitionCN: 对思想、标记、设计或其他受法律保护的无形之物的所有权
senses.example: A song can be property even though nothing physical is held.
senses.exampleCN: 一首歌可以是财产，尽管手中并未握着任何实体。
senses.why: If ownership is a legal relation rather than a physical grip, it can attach to what cannot be touched.
senses.whyCN: 如果所有权是一种法律关系而不是一把握持，它就能附着在摸不到的东西上。

senses.title: Objects used on a stage
senses.definition: the movable articles that an actor handles in a play or film
senses.definitionCN: 演员在戏剧或影片中操作的可移动物件
senses.example: The props master checks every property before the curtain rises.
senses.exampleCN: 道具管理员在幕启前检查每一件道具。
senses.why: The theatre borrowed the legal word for 'things owned by the company', shortened it, and kept the sense of objects that belong to a production.
senses.whyCN: 剧院借用了「剧团所有的物件」这一法律说法，把它缩短，保留了「属于某场演出之物」的意思。

senses.title: An attribute in logic and mathematics
senses.definition: a feature that may be predicated of an object, or a rule that a mathematical structure satisfies
senses.definitionCN: 可以述说某一对象的特征，或某一数学结构所满足的规则
senses.example: The proof uses a property shared by all prime numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 该证明用到所有素数共有的一个属性。
senses.why: The quality sense, pushed to its most abstract, becomes whatever can be said to belong to a class of objects.
senses.whyCN: 「性质」义被推到最抽象处，就成为一切可以说属于某类对象的特征。

senses.title: An estate or domain in older use
senses.definition: a landed estate with its house and lands, especially in historical and literary descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 连同宅邸与土地在内的地产，尤见于历史与文学描写
senses.example: The old property passed to the younger son.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧庄园传给了小儿子。
senses.why: Before land became a commodity it was an inherited domain, and that older meaning survives in descriptions of country estates.
senses.whyCN: 在土地成为商品之前，它是承袭而来的领地，这一较早的含义仍保留在对乡间地产的描写中。

intro.en: Property comes from Latin proprietas 'ownership, quality', from proprius 'one's own'. The deeper origin of proprius is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been suggested but not settled. English took the word through Old French.
intro.cn: property 出自拉丁语 proprietas「所有权、性质」，源头为 proprius「自己的」。proprius 的更深来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但未成定论。英语经古法语吸收此词。

items.en: Proprius meant 'one's own, particular, not shared'; its own origin is uncertain, and a derivation from a phrase meaning 'for the individual' has been proposed rather than proved.
items.cn: proprius 意为「自己的、特有的、不共享的」；它本身的来源不确定，有人认为它出自一个意为「为个体所有」的短语，但这只是提出而非证实。

items.en: Proprietas named both ownership and the quality that belongs to a thing, so the two later English senses were present from the start.
items.cn: proprietas 同时指所有权与某物固有的性质，因此后来英语中的两个义项从一开始就已存在。

items.en: Old French proprete carried both senses into English, where the legal and material side soon became dominant.
items.cn: 古法语 proprete 把两个义项都带入英语，其中法律与财物的一面很快占据主导。

items.en: In Middle English the word could still mean a quality, but land, goods and the right over them increasingly answered to it.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个词仍可指性质，但土地、货物以及对它们的权利越来越多地用它来表达。

items.en: In modern usage the material sense dominates law and everyday speech, while the quality sense survives mainly in science and logic. The date of this separation is approximate.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，财物义主导法律与日常表达，而性质义主要保存在科学与逻辑中。这一分家的年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is built on the same Latin adjective for 'one's own' but has drifted into fitness, decorum and exclusivity; the second group gives near alternatives for belongings and for qualities.
note.cn: 第一组由同一个表示「自己的」拉丁形容词构成，但已漂向合适、得体与独占；第二组是「财物」与「性质」两个方向的近义替代。

entries.definition: Correct or suitable, and in some phrases meaning 'itself'; the sense moved from 'belonging to a thing' to 'fitting that thing'.
entries.definitionCN: 正确的、合适的，在某些短语中意为「本身」；语义由「属于某物」转为「合乎某物」。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour or of usage; it comes from the same source but describes what is fitting rather than what is owned.
entries.definitionCN: 行为或用语得体；它出自同一来源，但描述合乎礼仪之事，而不是被拥有之物。

entries.definition: Owned by a particular person or firm, or sold under an exclusive name; it is the adjective built on the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由特定个人或公司所有的，或以独占名称销售的；它是建立在所有权义上的形容词。

entries.definition: The plural means several pieces of real estate or several qualities; the theatre shortening props belongs here too.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式可指数处房产或数种性质；剧院用语中的缩略形式也归在这里。

entries.definition: The fact of having something in one's control; it can exist without legal ownership, which is why the two are distinguished in law.
entries.definitionCN: 某物处于某人控制之下的事实；它可以没有法律上的所有权而存在，因此法律上把两者区分开。

entries.definition: Anything of value owned, seen from the balance sheet; it is a financial category rather than a legal relation.
entries.definitionCN: 所拥有的任何有价值之物，从资产负债表的角度看；它是一个财务类别，而不是法律关系。

entries.definition: A large area of land with a house, or the total property a person leaves at death; it is narrower than the entry word.
entries.definitionCN: 带有宅邸的大片土地，或某人去世时留下的全部财产；它比本词窄。

entries.definition: A characteristic regarded as belonging to a person or thing; it covers the quality sense of the entry word but never the ownership sense.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为属于某人或某物的特征；它覆盖本词的性质义，却从不覆盖所有权义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin adjective for 'one's own', real derived words and real legal phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词、真实派生词与真实法律用语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Everything starts from the question 'whose is it', which is what 'one's own' answers.
normal.cn: 一切都从「这是谁的」这个问题开始，而「自己的」正是它的答案。

normal.en: The family runs proper, propriety, proprietor, proprietary and proprietorship.
normal.cn: 同族词包括恰当的、得体、所有人、专有的与所有权。

normal.en: The same word covers the object and the right over it, so lawyers speak of property in property.
normal.cn: 同一个词既覆盖物，也覆盖对物的权利，因此法学家会说对财产享有财产权。

normal.en: Land is the clearest property because it cannot be carried away.
normal.cn: 土地是最清楚的财产，因为它搬不走。

normal.en: The theatre shortened the word to props, and the stage sense is still alive.
normal.cn: 剧院把这个词缩短为「道具」，舞台义至今仍活在使用中。

abstract.en: Picture a stone at the edge of a field with a name cut into it, and a chair, a cup and a coat laid beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象田野边缘一块刻着名字的石头，旁边摆着一把椅子、一只杯子和一件外套。

abstract.en: Picture a transparent box around an idea, marked with the same seal as the house.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明的盒子罩住一个想法，盒上盖着与房屋相同的印章。

abstract.en: Picture a substance whose label reads not 'mine' but 'this is what I am like'.
abstract.cn: 想象一种物质的标签上写的不是「我的」，而是「我本来就是这样」。

examples.en: The firm owns property in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市拥有房产。

examples.en: Hardness is a property that the alloy keeps at high temperature.
examples.cn: 硬度是这种合金在高温下仍保持的一种性质。

examples.en: The lease set out who was responsible for repairs to the property.
examples.cn: 租约列明了谁负责该房产的修缮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「破坡地」——坡上那块地也是家产；再记住同一词还能指物之本性，就像地有坡、铁有硬。

root: 拉丁语 proprius「自己的、特有的」→ proprietas「所有权、性质」→ 经古法语 proprete 进入英语。proprius 的更深来源不确定，出自「为个体所有」短语的说法属假说；同根词包括 proper、propriety、proprietor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight readings grow from what answers 'whose is it'. The owned things come first, with land and buildings as the clearest case; then the right of ownership itself, which can attach even to untouchable things; then the quality that belongs to a thing, at home in science and logic; and finally the stage objects and the older landed estate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「这是谁的」这一答案长出。先是被拥有的东西，其中土地与房屋最清楚；其次是对物享有所有权的权利，它甚至可以附着在摸不到的东西上；再其次是某物固有的性质，在科学与逻辑中安家；最后是舞台道具与较早的地产庄园义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boundary stone with a name on it, and the things inside the line that answer to that name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块刻着名字的地界石，以及界线之内属于这个名字的一切。

branches.en: THINGS: belongings in general, and the objects a theatre company owns for a production.
branches.cn: 物：一般意义上的财物，以及剧团为某场演出所拥有的物件。

branches.en: LAND: the immovable core, houses and plots that cannot be carried off.
branches.cn: 土地：不可移动的内核，搬不走的房屋与地块。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: ownership as a legal power, extending to intangibles such as songs and marks.
branches.cn: 权利：作为法律权力的所有权，可延伸到歌曲与标记等无形之物。

branches.en: QUALITY: what belongs to a thing's nature, in the laboratory and in logic.
branches.cn: 性质：属于某物本性的东西，在实验室里也在逻辑中。

branches.en: ESTATE: the older landed domain, inherited rather than traded.
branches.cn: 庄园：较早的领地，承袭而来而非买卖所得。

intro.en: One Latin adjective for 'one's own' supplies the whole family, with noun and agent endings added; the sense splits between what is owned and what a thing is like.
intro.cn: 一个表示「自己的」的拉丁形容词提供了整个家族，随后加上名词与施事后缀；语义在「被拥有之物」与「某物像什么」之间分开。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms below show the adjective, its abstract noun and the neuter form used as a noun.
latinIntro.cn: 下列拉丁形式展示了这个形容词、它的抽象名词，以及作名词用的中性形式。

items.example: The property passed to the eldest child.
The two properties share a fence.
items.exampleCN: 这两处房产共用一道篱笆。

items.example: That is the proper way to fold the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 那才是折这块布的正确方法。

items.example: The machine must be properly sealed.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器必须妥善密封。

items.example: The guests observed the proprieties of the house.
items.exampleCN: 客人们遵守这户人家的礼节。

items.meaning: the owner of a business or estate
items.example: The proprietor greeted us at the door.
The software is proprietary and cannot be copied.
items.exampleCN: 该软件为专有软件，不得复制。

items.example: The business is under sole proprietorship.

items.meaning: to take as one's own; suitable
items.example: The council appropriated funds for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 议会拨出款项用于这座桥。

latinEntries.meaning: a thing of one's own; a characteristic

derivatives.zh: 所有人；业主（表示「自己的」词根加表施事的名词后缀，指对某物享有所有权的人）
专有的；所有权的（名词加形容词后缀，指由某一所有人独占或与其所有权相关）
所有权；业主身份（名词加表身份或状态的名词后缀，指作为所有人的地位）
恰当的；本身的（由拉丁语中表示「自己的」形容词经法语传入，语义由「属于自己的」转为「合乎其本性的」）

definition_zh: 金属；金属材料；铁轨；重金属音乐
definition_en: a solid element or material such as iron, copper or gold, usually shiny and able to conduct heat and electricity; also a railway term and a music genre
core_image: 磁铁吊起一堆压扁的铁皮，金属在灯下泛出冷硬的光
scene: 天快黑的废料场里，吊臂上的磁铁把压扁的车壳吸到半空，铁皮互相碰撞发出脆响。 A magnet lifted the crushed metal above the scrapyard.
sceneCN: 这里是「金属」（第 1 个义项：有光泽、能导电的元素）；句意为磁铁把压扁的金属吸到废料场上空。图中可辨识物件：磁铁吊臂、压扁的车壳、废料场。

pos.zh: 金属；金属材料；铁轨；重金属音乐

derivatives.zh: 由 metal 加 -ic 构成，义为「金属的；有金属光泽的」
由 metal 词干与希腊语表示「工作」的词组合，义为「冶金学」
由 metal 与 work 复合，义为「金属加工；金属制品」

senses.title: A class of shiny, workable elements
senses.definition: a chemical element such as iron, copper or gold that is usually shiny, conducts heat and electricity, and can be shaped
senses.definitionCN: 铁、铜、金一类通常有光泽、能导热导电、可加工成型的化学元素
senses.example: Iron and copper are the metals most often used in wiring and tools.
senses.exampleCN: 铁和铜是最常用于电线和工具的金属。
senses.why: Greek metallon first named what miners dug out of the earth, so the word began as the stuff of mines rather than as a chemical class; shine and weight were noticed afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 metallon 最初指矿工从地下挖出的东西，所以这个词的起点是「矿井的产出」，而不是化学分类；光泽与重量是后来才被注意到的特征。

senses.title: The material used for making things
senses.definition: the solid material obtained from such elements or their alloys, used to make tools, machines and structures
senses.definitionCN: 由这类元素或其合金得到的固态材料，用来制作工具、机器和建筑结构
senses.example: The old gate is solid metal, so it will not burn.
senses.exampleCN: 这扇旧门是实心金属做的，所以烧不起来。
senses.why: Once metallon named the mined substance, speakers could treat it as a mass that gates and engines are made of, so the word came to name raw material rather than a list of elements.
senses.whyCN: 既然 metallon 指采出的那种物质，说话人就能把它当成造门、造机器的「料」，于是词义落在原料上，而不是一份元素清单。

senses.title: Railway rails, in British usage
senses.definition: the steel rails of a railway line, usually in the plural in British railway talk
senses.definitionCN: 铁路线上的钢轨，通常用复数，是英国铁路行业的说法
senses.example: The signal failed, and the train stopped on the metals.
senses.exampleCN: 信号失灵，列车停在了铁轨上。
senses.why: Rails are the heaviest pieces of metal a passenger ever rides over, so railway talk lets the material stand in for the object made from it.
senses.whyCN: 钢轨是乘客每天压过的最重的金属件，铁路行话便用材料名代替成品，直接把它叫作 metals。

senses.title: Heavy metal music
senses.definition: a loud genre of rock music, short for heavy metal, built on distorted guitars and heavy drumming
senses.definitionCN: 一种喧闹的摇滚乐类型，是 heavy metal 的简称，以失真吉他和沉重鼓点为主
senses.example: He grew up on metal and still keeps the old records.
senses.exampleCN: 他听重金属长大，至今还留着那些旧唱片。
senses.why: The music imitates the weight of dense metal in sound, so the genre borrowed the material name to describe how it feels rather than what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: 这种音乐用声音模仿致密金属的重量感，于是曲风借用材料名来描述听感，而不是描述材质。

intro.en: Metal travelled from a Greek word for a mine through Latin and French before English used it for the shiny substance and then for a music genre.
intro.cn: metal 从一个表示「矿井」的希腊词出发，经拉丁语与法语进入英语，先指那种发亮的物质，后来又指一种音乐类型。

items.en: Metallon covered a mine, the ore dug from it and the metal smelted out of it; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: metallon 兼指矿井、采出的矿石和冶炼出的金属；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as metallum and kept both the mining and the metal senses.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊名词写作 metallum，同时保留采矿与金属两层意思。

items.en: Old French passed metal to English as the name of the substance, stripped of the mine.
items.cn: 古法语把 metal 传给英语，只留下「物质」这一层，矿井的意思脱落了。

items.en: Middle English metal named the substance and also a person's temper, the two uses sharing one spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语的 metal 既指金属，也指人的性情，两种用法共用一个拼写。

items.en: Modern English split the spellings: metal kept the material, mettle kept the courage, and later the word was extended to rails and to heavy music.
items.cn: 现代英语把拼写分开：metal 保留材料义，mettle 保留勇气义；后来词义又扩展到铁轨与重金属音乐。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers relatives built on the Greek and Latin metal stem; the near-meaning group gathers other words for metals and metal-bearing rock.
note.cn: 形近组收希腊语与拉丁语 metal 词干上的同族词；近义组收其他表示金属与含金属矿石的词。

entries.definition: Made of metal, or bright and hard like it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属制的，或像金属一样光亮坚硬。

entries.definition: The science of getting metal from ore and preparing it for use.
entries.definitionCN: 从矿石中提取金属并加以处理的技术。

entries.definition: Courage and spirit; a doublet whose spelling split off from metal.
entries.definitionCN: 勇气与气概；拼写从 metal 分化出来的同源词。

entries.definition: An element whose properties sit between metals and non-metals.
entries.definitionCN: 性质介于金属与非金属之间的元素。

entries.definition: A hard, heavy metal used for tools and structures.
entries.definitionCN: 一种坚硬沉重的金属，用于工具和建筑。

entries.definition: An alloy of iron and carbon, stronger and harder than iron.
entries.definitionCN: 铁与碳的合金，比铁更硬更强。

entries.definition: A metal made by melting two or more metals together.
entries.definitionCN: 把两种或多种金属熔合而成的金属。

entries.definition: Rock or earth from which metal can be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 可以从中提取金属的矿石或泥土。

normalIntro.en: The word came out of the mine, and its family keeps splitting into material, craft, courage and sound.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词出自矿井，它的同族一路分到材料、工艺、勇气和声音。

normal.en: Greek metallon named what miners dug out, so metal began as the stuff of mines rather than a chemical category.
normal.cn: 希腊语 metallon 指矿工挖出来的东西，所以 metal 起初是矿井的产出，而不是化学分类。

normal.en: Mettle is the same word with a different spelling: the courage sense kept the old form while metal kept the material sense.
normal.cn: mettle 是同一个词的另一种拼写：勇气义保留了旧形，metal 则保留材料义。

normal.en: Metallic adds -ic, the suffix that turns a noun into the meaning relating to metal.
normal.cn: metallic 加的是 -ic，这个后缀把名词变成「与金属有关的」。

normal.en: Metallurgy joins metal to the Greek word for work, so the name says working metal rather than merely having it.
normal.cn: metallurgy 把 metal 与希腊语中表示「工作」的词结合，名字强调对金属的加工，而不是拥有金属。

normal.en: Heavy metal takes the weight of the material into music, which is why the genre is described as dense and loud.
normal.cn: heavy metal 把材料的重量带进音乐，所以这种曲风被形容为致密、喧闹。

abstract.en: Picture a mine, a furnace and a rail: one substance travelling from rock to engine.
abstract.cn: 想象矿井、熔炉和铁轨：同一种物质从岩石一路走到发动机上。

abstract.en: A word for a chemical element can also name a music genre, which shows how far a material word can drift into sound.
abstract.cn: 一个表示化学元素的词也能指一种音乐类型，可见材料词能漂移到多远的声音领域。

abstract.en: Every trusted tool is a lump of metal someone shaped, and the word still carries that dependence.
abstract.cn: 每件可信赖的工具都曾是某人塑形的一块金属，这个词仍带着这份依赖。

examples.en: The magnet lifted the crushed metal out of the pile.
examples.cn: 磁铁把压扁的金属从废料堆里吸了出来。

examples.en: Copper is a metal that carries electricity well.
examples.cn: 铜是一种导电性很好的金属。

examples.en: The band plays metal every Friday night.
examples.cn: 这支乐队每周五夜里都演奏重金属。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卖铁」——收废品的人一喊卖铁，卖的就是一堆金属；记住 metal 是金属。

root: 希腊语 metallon（矿井、金属）经拉丁语 metallum 与古法语 metal 进入英语；同族词多与金属、冶金有关，另有拼写分化的 mettle 表示勇气。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the mined substance; from it the senses run to the material, to the rails made of it, and finally to a music named after its weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是矿井里采出的那种物质；义项由此走向材料、走向用材料铺成的铁轨，最后走向以它的重量命名的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnet lifting crushed steel, the metal cold and bright under the yard lights.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁铁吊起压扁的钢壳，金属在废料场的灯下又冷又亮。

branches.en: a magnet lifting crushed cars in a scrapyard
branches.cn: 废料场上磁铁吊起压扁的车壳

branches.en: a steel girder holding up a motorway
branches.cn: 撑起高速公路的钢梁

branches.en: a train waiting on the rails at a red signal
branches.cn: 红灯前停在铁轨上的列车

branches.en: a wall of speakers at a loud concert
branches.cn: 喧闹演出里的一整面音箱墙

branches.en: one substance running from the mine to the machine
branches.cn: 同一种物质从矿井一路走到机器上

intro.en: The word rests on a Greek mine-word and its Latin borrowing, with two English suffixes and a compound that carry the family outward.
intro.cn: 这个词立在希腊语表示矿井的词及其拉丁借词上，再由两个英语后缀和一个复合词把词族向外撑开。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 性质介于金属与非金属之间的元素

definition_zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（计算机）病毒；恶毒影响
definition_en: a tiny agent that lives inside cells and makes copies of itself, often causing disease
core_image: 一个带刺的小球贴在细胞门口，正准备钻进去复制自己
scene: 一月的急诊室里，孩子的体温降不下来，医生先排除了细菌。 The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
sceneCN: 这里 virus 是「病毒」（第 1 个义项：寄生在细胞里、复制自身并能致病的微小因子）；句意为医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。贴到细胞门口的那个带刺小球，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（电脑）病毒；恶毒影响

derivatives.zh: 由 virus 加 -al 构成，义为「病毒的； viral 式的」
vir 与 -ology 复合，义为「病毒学」
加 -ist 构成，义为「病毒学家」
同出拉丁词根，义为「剧毒的；恶毒的」

senses.title: A tiny disease agent
senses.definition: an infective agent too small to be seen under a normal microscope, multiplying only inside living cells
senses.definitionCN: 小到普通显微镜看不见，只能在活细胞内复制繁殖的感染因子
senses.example: The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。
senses.why: Latin virus meant poison or slime, and when scientists found an agent smaller than bacteria they gave it that old name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virus 意为毒液、黏液，科学家发现一种比细菌更小的因子时，就给它用了这个旧名。

senses.title: An illness caused by it
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a sickness thought to come from such an agent
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指由这类因子引起的病
senses.example: He has been off work for a week with a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为一次病毒感染病休了一周。
senses.why: People name the illness after its cause, so a viral cold is simply called a virus.
senses.whyCN: 人们以病因称呼疾病，病毒性感冒就被直接叫作 a virus。

senses.title: A program that spreads itself
senses.definition: a hidden program that copies itself into other programs and damages them
senses.definitionCN: 能把自己复制到别的程序中、并造成破坏的隐藏程序
senses.example: The old laptop was slow because of a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧笔记本因为中了病毒而变慢。
senses.why: A computer virus spreads and multiplies like the biological one, so the borrowed name needed no change.
senses.whyCN: 电脑病毒像生物病毒一样传播、复制，借来的名字不必改动。

senses.title: A harmful influence
senses.definition: in literary use, something that corrupts a mind or a society
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法中指腐蚀人心或社会的东西
senses.example: The writer called envy a virus of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 那位作家把嫉妒称为精神上的病毒。
senses.why: Poison spreading unseen is an old image for bad influence, which explains the literary sense.
senses.whyCN: 看不见地扩散的毒，是描述恶劣影响的旧意象，文学义由此而来。

senses.title: Poison in the old sense
senses.definition: in Latin and early English, a poisonous liquid or a foul humour
senses.definitionCN: 在拉丁语与早期英语里指毒液或有毒的体液
senses.example: Old medicine blamed a virus in the blood for the swelling.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医学把这种肿痛归咎于血液中的毒。
senses.why: Before viruses were seen, the word named any poison, and trace of that sense survives in virulent.
senses.whyCN: 在病毒被看见之前，这个词泛指任何毒，这层意思还留在 virulent 里。

intro.en: Virus is Latin for poison or slime, and science borrowed it as a technical term only in modern times.
intro.cn: virus 在拉丁语里指毒液或黏液，科学界只是在近代才把它借作术语。

items.en: Virus meant a poisonous liquid, slime or a foul discharge.
items.cn: virus 意为毒液、黏液或恶臭的分泌物。

items.en: English used it for poison in the seventeenth century, mostly in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪用它表示毒，主要用于科学写作。

items.en: After filters caught bacteria but not the smaller agent, virus was used for the new class.
items.cn: 过滤器能拦住细菌却拦不住更小的因子后，virus 被用来指这一新类别。

items.en: Electron microscopes made the particles visible in the nineteen thirties.
items.cn: 三十年代的电子显微镜使这些颗粒变得可见。

items.en: Computer use in the nineteen seventies and the adjective viral in the internet age added new branches.
items.cn: 七十年代的电脑用法与互联网时代的形容词 viral 又添了新枝。

note.en: The first group follows the family and the look-alike, the second the words for germs and their effects.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与形近词，第二组收病菌及其影响类词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning of a virus, or spreading fast online.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「病毒的、在网上迅速传播的」。

entries.definition: The scientific study of viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 研究病毒的学科。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same Latin root meaning very poisonous or bitter.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「剧毒的、恶毒的」。

entries.definition: Single-celled organisms that can also cause disease, larger than viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 单细胞生物，也能致病，比病毒大。

entries.definition: An everyday word for any microbe that spreads disease.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，泛指致病微生物。

entries.definition: The condition caused when an agent enters the body.
entries.definitionCN: 病原进入身体后造成的状况。

entries.definition: An adjective for diseases spread from person to person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容疾病在人际传播。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word for poison serves a microbe, a sickness, a program and a bad idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁的「毒」字，同时服务微生物、一场病、一个程序与一个坏念头。

normal.en: Virus and virulent share a Latin root meaning poison.
normal.cn: virus 与 virulent 同出拉丁「毒」字词根。

normal.en: The plural is viruses; the adjective is viral.
normal.cn: 复数是 viruses，形容词是 viral。

normal.en: A virus needs a living cell; bacteria do not.
normal.cn: 病毒需要活细胞，细菌不需要。

normal.en: A computer virus copies itself into other programs, just as the biological one does.
normal.cn: 电脑病毒如生物病毒一样把自己复制进别的程序。

normal.en: Viral also means spreading fast on the internet.
normal.cn: viral 还指在网上迅速传播。

abstract.en: See a spiky ball landing on a cell wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带刺小球落在细胞壁上。

abstract.en: Hear a doctor say it is a virus, so an antibiotic will not help.
abstract.cn: 听医生说这是病毒，抗生素没用。

abstract.en: Picture a line of code quietly copying itself into a file.
abstract.cn: 想象一行代码悄悄把自己复制进一个文件。

examples.en: A virus cannot multiply without a living cell.
examples.cn: 病毒没有活细胞就不能繁殖。

examples.en: Most winter viruses spread through the air.
examples.cn: 多数冬季病毒通过空气传播。

examples.en: He lost all his files to a virus.
examples.cn: 一次病毒让他的文件全丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪螺」——长得歪歪扭扭的螺丝状小球，专往细胞里钻。

root: 拉丁语 virus（毒液、黏液）→ 科学拉丁语 virus（病毒）→ 英语 virus；同根词有 virulent。

sensesIntro.en: A Latin word for poison ends up meaning the smallest cause of illness, then the illness, then a program, then a harmful idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁的「毒」先是变成最小的病因，再变成那场病、那个程序，最后变成一个有害念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spiked particle landing on a cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：落在细胞上的带刺颗粒。

branches.en: The agent branch: a virus rather than bacteria.
branches.cn: 病原分支：是病毒而非细菌。

branches.en: The illness branch: off work for a week with a virus.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：因病毒感染病休一周。

branches.en: The computer branch: a laptop slowed by a virus.
branches.cn: 电脑分支：被病毒弄慢的笔记本。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: envy as a virus of the mind.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：嫉妒是精神的病毒。

branches.en: The old branch: a poison in the blood.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：血中的毒。

intro.en: Vir- carries the Latin poison; -us was the Latin ending, and -al, -ology, -ist build modern words.
intro.cn: vir- 携带拉丁的「毒」，-us 是拉丁词尾，-al、-ology、-ist 搭出现代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virus is recorded for a poison or a slime; the adjective virulentus is also recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virus 有毒液、黏液义都有记录，形容词 virulentus 同样有记录。

items.exampleCN: 这个名词是拉丁词，不是新造词。

items.exampleCN: 该词尾保留了拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 边缘；页边空白；差额；余地；利润空间；保证金
definition_en: the edge of an area, the blank space around printed text, the amount by which one thing differs from another, or the spare room kept for safety or profit
core_image: 纸页四周留出的白边：文字被围在中央，四周空着，可以写批注，也可以留作退路
scene: 编辑把校样摊在桌上。 She wrote a note in red in the right margin, asking the author to delete a repeated sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 margin 是「页边空白」（第 2 个义项：书页文字四周的空白）；句意：她在右侧页边空白处用红笔写下一行批注，请作者删去重复的句子。图中可辨识物件：校样纸、红色批注、页边白区、钢笔；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The edge of a physical area
senses.definition: the outer edge or border of a sea, lake, forest, field, or other area
senses.definitionCN: 海、湖、森林、田野或其他区域的外缘或边界
senses.example: Tall reeds grow along the margin of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 高高的芦苇长在湖的边缘。
senses.why: Margin is first recorded in the mid-14c. as 'edge of a sea or lake'. Latin margo meant 'edge, brink, border', so the word starts at the outermost line where one area stops and another begins.
senses.whyCN: margin 最早记录于 14 世纪中期，意为“海或湖的边缘”。拉丁语 margo 意为“边缘、崖边、边界”，因此这个词的起点是一个区域终止、另一个区域开始的那条最外线。

senses.title: The blank space around a page of text
senses.definition: the blank space between a block of text and the edge of a page
senses.definitionCN: 一块文字与纸张边缘之间的空白区域
senses.example: She wrote questions in the margin beside each paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每段旁边的页边空白处写下问题。
senses.why: By the late 14c. the word was used for the space between text and the edge of a leaf or sheet. The margin is not where writing ends but the reserved emptiness around it, which is why notes can later be added there.
senses.whyCN: 到 14 世纪晚期，这个词已用于指文字与纸页边缘之间的空间。页边不是文字结束的地方，而是文字周围被预留的空白，因此后来可以在那里加批注。

senses.title: The gap that decides a contest
senses.definition: the amount by which one competitor, result, or number is greater or smaller than another
senses.definitionCN: 一个竞争者、结果或数字比另一个大或小的量
senses.example: The bill passed by a margin of three votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案以三票的差距通过。
senses.why: Two results sit side by side, and the margin is the strip of space between them. A narrow margin means the strip is thin, so the outcome could easily have gone the other way.
senses.whyCN: 两个结果并排放着，margin 就是两者之间那条空隙。narrow margin 意味着这条缝隙很窄，所以结果很容易倒向另一边。

senses.title: Spare room kept for safety
senses.definition: an amount of time, money, or tolerance kept free so that unexpected problems can be absorbed
senses.definitionCN: 预留出的时间、金钱或容差，用来吸收意外问题
senses.example: Leave a margin of ten minutes before the connecting train.
senses.exampleCN: 给换乘列车留出十分钟的余量。
senses.why: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, provision for extended action' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. A page margin protects the text; a safety margin protects the plan.
senses.whyCN: “舒适的余量、缓冲、活动空间、为扩大行动所作的预留”这一义项记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。页边保护文字，安全余量保护计划。

senses.title: The strip between cost and price
senses.titleCN: 成本与售价之间的那一条
senses.definition: the difference between the cost of producing or buying something and the price at which it is sold
senses.definitionCN: 生产或购买某物的成本与售价之间的差额
senses.example: The bakery survives on a thin profit margin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店靠很薄的利润空间维持。
senses.why: In business the two sides of the page become cost and price, and the margin is the space between them. A thin margin leaves little room for error, which connects the financial sense back to the safety sense.
senses.whyCN: 在商业里，纸页的两边变成成本与售价，margin 就是两者之间的空间。薄利意味着几乎没有犯错的余地，这把金融义重新连回“安全余量”义。

senses.title: Collateral deposited with a broker
senses.definition: money deposited with a broker to cover the risk of loss when buying securities or goods on credit
senses.definitionCN: 以保证金方式买证券或货物时，交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的钱
senses.example: He bought the shares on margin and had to add cash after the drop.
senses.exampleCN: 他以保证金买进股票，股价下跌后不得不追加现金。
senses.why: The stock-market sense is recorded from 1848. The deposit is a buffer placed between the trader and a possible loss, exactly like the blank space that keeps the text from the edge.
senses.whyCN: 股市义记录于 1848 年。这笔押金是放在交易者与可能亏损之间的缓冲，和把文字与纸边隔开的空白完全同构。

senses.title: The edge of society: unimportant position
senses.titleCN: 社会的边缘：不重要的位置
senses.definition: a position at the edge of a group or society, with little influence or recognition
senses.definitionCN: 处于群体或社会边缘的位置，影响力或受认可度很低
senses.example: The report focuses on families living on the margins of the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告关注生活在城市边缘的家庭。
senses.why: A page has a centre and a margin, and a society can be imagined the same way. The adjective marginal, 'of little effect or importance', is recorded from 1887, so the spatial word becomes a social judgement.
senses.whyCN: 一页纸有中心也有页边，一个社会也可以被这样想象。形容词 marginal“影响很小、不重要”记录于 1887 年，于是空间词变成了社会判断。

senses.title: To write in the margin
senses.definition: to add notes in the margin of a page, or to provide something with a margin
senses.definitionCN: 在书页边缘添加批注，或给某物留出边
senses.example: The student margined every chapter with questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学生在每一章的页边都写满了问题。
senses.why: The verb appears c. 1600 as 'to furnish with marginal notes', and from 1715 as 'to furnish with a margin'. The place becomes an action: the blank strip is put to use.
senses.whyCN: 动词义约在 1600 年出现，意为“加页边注”，1715 年起又表示“给……留边”。地点变成了动作：那条空白被用起来了。

senses.title: Usage boundary: margin is not edge, profit, or leeway
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：margin 不等于 edge、profit 或 leeway
senses.definition: margin usually implies reserved or measured space, not a hard boundary; profit margin is a ratio, not the profit itself; margins in finance are collateral, not earnings
senses.definitionCN: margin 通常暗示被预留或被量出的空间，而不是硬边界；profit margin 是比率，不是利润本身；金融里的 margins 是保证金，不是收益
senses.example: The company's margin is thin, but its total profit is still large.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的利润率很薄，但利润总额仍然很大。
senses.why: Edge is simply where something stops; margin is the strip left around it. Profit is the money kept; a profit margin is the proportion that money represents. Keeping these apart prevents 'a large margin' from being read as 'a large profit'.
senses.whyCN: edge 只是某物终止的地方；margin 是围绕它留下的那一条。profit 是留下的钱；profit margin 是这笔钱所占的比例。分清这些，才不会把“a large margin”误读成“a large profit”。

intro.en: Margin began as the physical edge of water or land, then became the blank strip around printed text. From that strip came the ideas of a gap between results, spare room for safety, and the difference between cost and price.
intro.cn: margin 最初指水域或陆地的实体边缘，随后变成印刷文字四周的空白条。从这条空白又衍生出结果之间的差距、为安全预留的余量，以及成本与售价之间的差额。

items.en: First recorded as 'edge of a sea or lake', from Old French margin and directly from Latin marginem (nominative margo) 'edge, brink, border, margin'.
items.cn: 最早记录为“海或湖的边缘”，来自古法语 margin，并直接来自拉丁语 marginem（主格 margo）“边缘、崖边、边界、页边”。

items.en: The sense 'space between a block of text and the edge of a leaf or sheet' appears. The general sense 'bordering space, boundary space, rim or edge' follows in the same period.
items.cn: “文字块与纸页边缘之间的空间”义出现。“边界空间、边缘、外缘”的一般义也在同一时期出现。

items.en: margo is traced to PIE *merg- 'boundary, border'. The reconstruction is generally accepted; the root is also associated with mark and march, though those reach English by other routes.
items.cn: margo 被追溯到原始印欧语 *merg-“边界、边缘”。这一重构属于一般认为；该词根也与 mark、march 有关，但后两者经其他路径进入英语。

items.en: The stock-market sense 'sum deposited with a broker to cover risk of loss' is recorded from 1848, the earliest of the modern figurative senses.
items.cn: 股市义“交给经纪人以覆盖亏损风险的押金”记录于 1848 年，是现代引申义中最早的一个。

items.en: The sense 'comfort allowance, cushion, scope, range' is recorded by 1851, and margin of error by 1889. Marginal, 'of little effect or importance', follows in 1887.
items.cn: “舒适余量、缓冲、活动空间、范围”义记录于 1851 年，margin of error 记录于 1889 年。marginal“影响很小、不重要”随后于 1887 年出现。

items.en: Modern English keeps the page sense, adds profit margin and social margins, and keeps the verb meaning 'to annotate'. The core idea is always reserved space between two things.
items.cn: 现代英语保留页边义，增加利润率与社会边缘义，并保留动词“加旁注”义。核心始终是两样东西之间被预留的空间。

note.en: The first group is built on margo or the margin shape. The second group separates the physical edge, the dividing line, the financial gain and the freedom to act.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 margo 或 margin 词形上。第二组区分实体边缘、分界线、财务收益与行动自由。

entries.definition: written in a margin, at the edge, or too small to matter. It is the adjective from margin, recorded from the 1570s.
entries.definitionCN: 写在页边的、位于边缘的，或小到不重要的。它是 margin 的形容词，记录于 16 世纪 70 年代。

entries.definition: notes written in the margins of a book. It is the plural of the Latin neuter marginalis.
entries.definitionCN: 写在书页边上的批注。它是拉丁语中性形式 marginalis 的复数。

entries.definition: a poetic or old-fashioned word for edge or margin. It is easily confused with margarine, which is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 诗歌或旧式用语中的“边缘”。它容易被误认成 margarine（人造黄油），后者与此无关。

entries.definition: the line where a surface ends. It is sharper and more literal than margin, which often implies a strip of reserved space.
entries.definitionCN: 一个表面终止的那条线。它比 margin 更锋利、更字面；margin 常暗示一条被预留的空间。

entries.definition: the line dividing two countries or regions. It is political or geographic, while margin is usually a space rather than a line.
entries.definitionCN: 分隔两国或两地区的界线。它是政治或地理的；margin 通常是空间，而不是一条线。

entries.definition: the money left after costs are paid. A profit margin is the ratio, not the sum, so the two are not interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 付完成本后剩下的钱。profit margin 是比率而不是金额，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: the freedom to act or to be late without punishment. Margin is the spare amount; leeway is the permission to use it.
entries.definitionCN: 行动的自由，或可迟到而不受罚的宽容度。margin 是预留的量；leeway 是使用这个量的许可。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: margo 'edge' gives margin and marginal; the blank strip on a page is the image behind every later financial and social sense.
normalIntro.cn: 真实构词与真实同族词：margo“边缘”给出 margin 与 marginal；纸页上的空白条是后来所有金融义与社会义的底层意象。

normal.en: Look at a printed page: the text sits in the middle and a white strip runs around it. That strip is the margin, and every other sense is a version of it.
normal.cn: 看一页印刷纸：文字在中间，四周有一条白边。那条白边就是 margin，其他所有义项都是它的变体。

normal.en: A margin of error is a white strip around a measurement; buy on margin is a cash strip around a risky trade.
normal.cn: margin of error 是测量结果四周的白边；buy on margin 是一笔风险交易四周的现金缓冲。

normal.en: Profit margin is the strip between cost and price, thin or wide. It is a ratio, not the money itself.
normal.cn: profit margin 是成本与售价之间的那一条，可宽可窄。它是比率，不是钱本身。

normal.en: On the margins of society means at the edge of the page, outside the main text.
normal.cn: on the margins of society 就是处在纸页边缘、正文之外。

normal.en: The verb margin means writing in that strip: the place turns into an action.
normal.cn: 动词 margin 就是在那一条上写字：地点变成了动作。

abstract.en: Picture every important thing with a strip of empty space around it: a page, a score, a budget, a life. Margin is that strip, and its width tells you how safe or how thin things are.
abstract.cn: 想象每一件要紧的东西四周都留有一条空白：一页纸、一场比分、一份预算、一段人生。margin 就是那条空白，它的宽度告诉你事情有多安全、有多紧。

abstract.en: When the strip is inside a system it is tolerance; when it is inside a business it is profit; when it is inside a society it is exclusion.
abstract.cn: 当这条空白在系统内部，它是容差；在商业内部，它是利润；在社会内部，它是排斥。

abstract.en: The margin is never the centre, but nothing at the centre can be measured without it.
abstract.cn: 页边永远不是中心，但中心的一切都离不开它才能被量出来。

examples.en: The village sits at the margin of the forest and the marsh.
examples.cn: 这个村子位于森林与沼泽的边缘。

examples.en: The team won by a margin of two goals.
examples.cn: 这支球队以两球的差距获胜。

examples.en: Small shops survive on narrow margins and loyal customers.
examples.cn: 小店靠薄利和忠实顾客维持。

dict_mnemonic.text: “马诊”——马医生在页边空白处记下诊断，留出余地再下结论 → margin 页边、余地、差额

root: 拉丁语 margo（属格 marginis）“边缘、边界”，核心是“中心之外的那一条空间”，由页边引申为差额、余地、利润与保证金。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of margin, all one strip of reserved space: the edge of land, the blank page, a winning gap, a safety cushion, a profit ratio, broker's collateral, social periphery, a marginal note, and the boundary against edge and profit.
sensesIntro.cn: margin 的九个义项都是同一条被预留的空间：土地边缘、页边空白、胜负差距、安全余量、利润比率、经纪人保证金、社会边缘、页边批注，以及它与 edge、profit 的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strip of empty space runs between the centre and the outer limit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条空白带介于中心与最外缘之间。

branches.en: LAND: the first sense is the physical rim where water, forest or field ends.
branches.cn: 土地：最早的义项是水域、森林或田野终止的实体外缘。

branches.en: PAGE: the blank strip around text, and the act of writing notes in it.
branches.cn: 纸页：文字四周的空白条，以及在其中写批注的动作。

branches.en: GAP: the measured space between two results is also the space kept free for safety.
branches.cn: 差距：两个结果之间被量出的空间，也是为安全而预留的空间。

branches.en: MONEY: cost and price leave a strip of profit; a broker holds a strip of collateral.
branches.cn: 金钱：成本与售价之间留下利润的那一条；经纪人手里握着保证金那一条。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND BOUNDARY: people at the edge of the page become marginal, and the strip is never a hard line.
branches.cn: 社会与边界：处在纸页边缘的人变成 marginal，而这条空白从不是一条硬线。

intro.en: Margin has no live English prefix. Its Latin stem margo, margin- is frozen inside; English adds -al, -ally, -alize and -alia to build the family.
intro.cn: margin 没有活的英语前缀。它的拉丁词干 margo、margin- 凝固在词内；英语加 -al、-ally、-alize、-alia 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: The *merg- 'boundary' root also underlies mark and march, which reached English through Germanic routes. Within English, the margin family is built on the Latin stem margin-.
latinIntro.cn: *merg-“边界”这个词根也支撑 mark 与 march，它们经日耳曼路径进入英语。在英语内部，margin 词族建立在拉丁词干 margin- 上。

items.meaning: written in a margin, situated at an edge, or small enough to be unimportant
items.meaningCN: 页边的；边缘的；微不足道的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The difference in cost is marginal.
items.exampleCN: 成本上的差别微不足道。

items.meaningCN: 略微；轻微地；在边缘地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The second design is marginally cheaper.
items.exampleCN: 第二个设计稍微便宜一点。

items.meaning: to push a person or group to the edge of influence
items.meaningCN: 使边缘化；把某人或群体排挤到影响力边缘（-ize 表示“使……化”）
items.example: Cheap transport marginalised the old market.
items.exampleCN: 廉价的交通让老市场边缘化了。

items.meaning: notes written in the margins of a book
items.meaningCN: 页边注；旁注（-ia 构成复数名词）
items.example: The library copy is full of marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆那本书上写满了旁注。

items.structure: Latin noun, third declension, genitive marginis
items.example: The noun is the direct source of margin.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 margin 的直接来源。

items.example: The stem appears in margin, marginal and marginalia.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干见于 margin、marginal 与 marginalia。

items.example: It forms marginal, belonging to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginal，即属于边缘的。

items.meaning: to make, to cause to be
items.example: It forms marginalize, to push to the edge.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalize，即把……推向边缘。

items.example: It forms marginalia, notes written in the margins.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 marginalia，即写在页边的批注。

latinEntries.meaning: the act of marking a boundary

latinEntries.meaningCN: 标记；界标（原指边界记号）

latinEntries.meaning: borderland; the boundary region between two countries

latinEntries.structure: Old French marchis (lord of a march) from marche (border)
latinEntries.meaning: a noble ranking below a duke, originally the lord of a border region
latinEntries.meaningCN: 侯爵（原指边境地区的领主）

definition_en: to make someone afraid, or to drive someone away by fear
core_image: 雷声响起，孩子猛地缩起肩膀
scene: 突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。 The sudden thunder frightened the child.
sceneCN: 这里 frighten 是「使惊吓」（第 1 个义项）；句意：突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。

derivatives.zh: 惊吓
害怕的
可怕的

senses.title: To make afraid
senses.definition: to make a person or animal feel fear
senses.definitionCN: 让人或动物感到恐惧
senses.example: The sudden thunder frightened the child.
senses.exampleCN: 突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。
senses.why: This is the basic action sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的动作义项。

senses.title: To drive away
senses.definition: to make a person or animal leave by fear
senses.definitionCN: 用恐惧把人或动物赶走
senses.example: The loud dog frightened the birds away.
senses.exampleCN: 大声吠叫的狗把鸟吓跑了。
senses.why: Fear becomes a force that moves others.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧变成推动他人离开的力量。

senses.title: To force by fear
senses.definition: to make someone do something through fear
senses.definitionCN: 通过恐惧使某人做某事
senses.example: They frightened him into signing the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他们吓得他签了文件。
senses.why: Fear can push a person into action.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧能推着人行动。

intro.en: Frighten is built on the old noun fright.
intro.cn: frighten 由古老名词 fright 加 -en 构成。

items.en: Fyrhto meant fear.
items.cn: fyrhto 意为恐惧。

items.en: Fright named sudden fear.
items.cn: fright 指突然的恐惧。

items.en: Frighten meant to cause fear.
items.cn: frighten 意为引起恐惧。

items.en: It also meant to scare away.
items.cn: 它也意为把……吓跑。

items.en: The adjective frightened became common.
items.cn: 形容词 frightened 变得常用。

note.en: Frighten is compared with similar-looking words and words for scaring.
note.cn: 把 frighten 与形近词以及表示惊吓的词作比较。

entries.definitionCN: 使明亮

entries.definition: to make tighter

normalIntro.en: Frighten puts fear into someone, or drives them away.
normalIntro.cn: frighten 把恐惧放进某人心里，或把人吓跑。

normal.en: The sudden thunder frightened the child.
normal.cn: 突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。

normal.en: The loud dog frightened the birds away.
normal.cn: 大声吠叫的狗把鸟吓跑了。

normal.en: They frightened him into signing the paper.
normal.cn: 他们吓得他签了文件。

normal.en: The dark hallway frightens the little dog.
normal.cn: 昏暗的走廊让小狗害怕。

normal.en: She was frightened of the deep water.
normal.cn: 她害怕深水。

abstract.en: Fear is a shadow that needs no body.
abstract.cn: 恐惧是一道不需要实体的影子。

abstract.en: To frighten is to lend your shadow to another.
abstract.cn: 吓人，就是把自己的影子借给别人。

abstract.en: Courage is fear that has decided to stay.
abstract.cn: 勇气是决定留下来的恐惧。

examples.en: The sudden thunder frightened the child.
examples.cn: 突如其来的雷声吓哭了孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: fright（惊吓）+ -en（使动词后缀）= frighten；be frightened of 表示「害怕」，frighten away 表示「吓跑」。

root: 由古英语 fyrhto（恐惧）演变的名词 fright 加动词后缀 -en 构成，核心义「使恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: Frighten means to make afraid, to drive away by fear, or to force by fear.
sensesIntro.cn: frighten 意为使惊吓、吓跑或吓得某人做某事。

core.en: Putting fear into another.
core.cn: 把恐惧放进他人心中。

branches.en: Thunder makes a child cry.
branches.cn: 雷声让孩子哭起来。

branches.en: A barking dog clears the birds.
branches.cn: 吠叫的狗把鸟赶走。

branches.en: Pressure makes a hand sign.
branches.cn: 压力迫使一只手签字。

branches.en: Fear can shake a person or move them away.
branches.cn: 恐惧能让人发抖，也能让人离开。

branches.en: Fear both drives away and drives into action.
branches.cn: 恐惧既能驱赶，也能驱使行动。

intro.en: Frighten builds words for fear and scary things.
intro.cn: frighten 构成表示恐惧与可怕事物的词。

latinIntro.en: Frighten is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: frighten 属日耳曼语，并非拉丁语。

items.example: The fright made her drop the cup.
The light frightened the fox away.

definition_en: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing, or to be a typical quality of something
core_image: 用几笔勾出一个人最显眼的轮廓
scene: 评论家用一个词概括这座城市的脾气。 Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
sceneCN: 这里 characterize 指「把…描绘成」（第 1 个义项：描述某物具有的特征）；句意是评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。

derivatives.zh: 性格；人物；字符
典型的；特有的
描绘；人物刻画

senses.title: To describe the nature of
senses.definition: to describe the typical qualities of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 描述某人或某物的典型品质
senses.example: Critics characterize the city as restless and young.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家把这座城市描绘成躁动而年轻。
senses.why: The Greek stem meant to stamp a mark, and describing someone is stamping a mark with words.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语词干意为压上记号，而描述一个人就是用词语压上记号。

senses.title: To be a typical mark of
senses.definition: to be a quality that marks a person, place or period
senses.definitionCN: 成为标志某人、某地或某时期的品质
senses.example: Long winters characterize the region.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的冬天是该地区的特点。
senses.why: The same stamp can be applied by the thing itself, so the verb also means to be the mark.
senses.whyCN: 同一枚印章也可以由事物自己盖上，于是这个动词也表示「就是那道记号」。

intro.en: Characterize adds the verb ending -ize to the Greek mark that gave character.
intro.cn: characterize 在给出 character 的希腊语记号后加上动词词尾 -ize。

items.en: Kharakter meant an engraved mark.
items.cn: 希腊语 kharakter 意为刻出的记号。

items.en: Character kept the sense of a distinctive sign.
items.cn: 拉丁语 character 保留独特记号的含义。

items.en: Caracteriser named the act of marking out a nature.
items.cn: caracteriser 指标示出某种本性的行为。

items.en: English characterize meant to describe the qualities of something.
items.cn: 英语 characterize 意为描述某物的品质。

items.en: The passive be characterized by now names a defining feature.
items.cn: 被动式 be characterized by 如今指某项决定性特征。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the character stem, while the meaning group lists verbs of describing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 character 词干，近义组列出描述类动词。

entries.definition: the nature of a person
entries.definitionCN: 一个人的本性

entries.definition: a typical feature
entries.definitionCN: 典型特征

entries.definition: described or marked in the past
entries.definitionCN: 过去被描述或标记的

entries.definition: to say what someone or something is like
entries.definitionCN: 说出某人或某物的样子

entries.definition: to show a person or thing in a certain way
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式表现人或事物

entries.definition: to state the exact nature of something
entries.definitionCN: 说明某物的确切性质

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the mark root, the -ize verb ending and the passive pattern be characterized by.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用记号词根、-ize 动词词尾以及被动句式 be characterized by。

normal.en: Characterize is character plus -ize, so it means to put the mark into words.
normal.cn: characterize 是 character 加 -ize，意思是用词语把记号说出来。

normal.en: Characterize as is the pattern for calling a thing a certain kind.
normal.cn: characterize as 是把某物称作某种样子的句式。

normal.en: Be characterized by reverses the view and names the mark itself.
normal.cn: be characterized by 把视角反过来，直接说出那道记号。

normal.en: Long winters characterize the region is a natural way to state a feature.
normal.cn: 长冬 characterize the region 是陈述特征的自然说法。

normal.en: The third person characterizes simply adds an s before the z sound.
normal.cn: 第三人称 characterizes 只在 z 音前加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a critic drawing three quick lines around a city.
abstract.cn: 想象评论家围着城市飞快画了三笔。

abstract.en: Picture a label being stuck on a whole season.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签被贴在整个季节上。

abstract.en: Picture a portrait that catches one crooked smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅肖像只抓住一个歪嘴的笑。

examples.en: The report characterizes the market as unstable.
examples.cn: 报告把市场描绘成不稳定的。

examples.en: Heavy rain characterizes the summer here.
examples.cn: 大雨是这里夏天的特点。

examples.en: Her work is characterized by sharp detail.
examples.cn: 她的作品以细节锐利为特征。

dict_mnemonic.text: characterize 是 character 加 -ize：把一个人的记号用词语盖出来，就是描绘他的特征。

root: 由 character（希腊语 kharakter，刻痕）加动词后缀 -ize 构成，核心是「压上记号」，引申为描述特征或以…为特征。

sensesIntro.en: Stamping a mark with words gives the describing sense, and being the mark itself gives the passive feature sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 用词语压上记号给出描述义，而自身就是那道记号则给出被动特征义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mark pressed onto a person or period.
core.cn: 核心意象：压在人身上或时代上的一个记号。

branches.en: Critics characterize a city by picking a few traits.
branches.cn: 评论家挑出几个特点来描绘一座城市。

branches.en: Long winters mark the whole region.
branches.cn: 漫长的冬天标记出整个地区。

branches.en: Characterize as fits reports and reviews.
branches.cn: characterize as 常见于报告与评论。

branches.en: Active and passive forms share one stamp.
branches.cn: 主动与被动形式共享同一枚印章。

branches.en: Be characterized by names the mark directly.
branches.cn: be characterized by 直接说出那道记号。

intro.en: Characterize combines the character stem with the verb suffix -ize.
intro.cn: characterize 把 character 词干与动词后缀 -ize 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The stem goes back to Greek kharakter, a mark cut into a surface.
latinIntro.cn: 词干可追溯到希腊语 kharakter，即刻入表面的记号。

items.exampleCN: 这种风格是她作品的特点。

items.example: The age was characterized by speed.
The character of the town changed.

definition_en: the money needed or spent for something; something that costs money; the loss or sacrifice involved
core_image: 为得到某样东西而付出的钱
scene: 他把差旅费用记在了公司账上。 He put the travel expenses on the company account.
sceneCN: 这里 expense 是「费用、开支」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把差旅费用记在了公司账上。

derivatives.zh: 花费；消耗
昂贵的
可消耗的

senses.title: Cost of something
senses.definition: the money needed or spent for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事物所需或所花的钱
senses.example: The expense of the trip was too high.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行的费用太高了。
senses.why: The base sense is money laid out.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是付出去的钱。

senses.title: Money for work
senses.definition: money spent for a particular purpose, often repaid by an employer
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途支出、常由雇主报销的钱
senses.example: She kept every receipt to claim her expenses.
senses.exampleCN: 她保留每张收据以便报销。
senses.why: The cost is tied to a job or purpose.
senses.whyCN: 费用与工作或特定用途绑定。

senses.title: Price paid
senses.definition: the loss or sacrifice involved in gaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而付出的损失或牺牲
senses.example: He won the race at the expense of his health.
senses.exampleCN: 他以健康为代价赢得了比赛。
senses.why: Money cost becomes any kind of cost.
senses.whyCN: 金钱成本扩展为任何代价。

intro.en: Expense comes from Latin expensa, money paid out.
intro.cn: expense 源自拉丁语 expensa，意为「付出去的钱」。

items.en: Expensa is money paid out.
items.cn: expensa 指付出去的钱。

items.en: Expendere means to weigh out and spend.
items.cn: expendere 意为称量后花费。

items.en: Espense keeps the sense of cost.
items.cn: espense 保留「花费」之义。

items.en: Expense enters as a business term.
items.cn: expense 作为商业用语进入英语。

items.en: Expense covers both cost and sacrifice.
items.cn: expense 同时涵盖费用与牺牲。

items.en: At the expense of is a fixed phrase.
items.cn: at the expense of 成为固定搭配。

note.en: Expense is money spent; an expanse is a wide area.
note.cn: expense 是花掉的钱，expanse 则是广阔区域。

entries.definition: a wide area of land or space
entries.definitionCN: 广阔区域

entries.definition: to use up money or energy
entries.definitionCN: 花费；耗尽

entries.definition: someone with special skill
entries.definitionCN: 专家

entries.definition: the amount paid for something
entries.definitionCN: 成本；费用

entries.definition: an amount asked for a service
entries.definitionCN: 收费

entries.definition: the money needed to buy something
entries.definitionCN: 价格；代价

normalIntro.en: Expense is what you pay in money or in other ways.
normalIntro.cn: expense 是你付出的钱或其他代价。

normal.en: The trip was worth the expense.
normal.cn: 这趟旅行花这些钱是值得的。

normal.en: They spared no expense on the wedding.
normal.cn: 他们为婚礼不惜花费。

normal.en: He learned the skill at the expense of his free time.
normal.cn: 他以牺牲空闲时间为代价学会了这项技能。

normal.en: Living expenses in the city keep rising.
normal.cn: 城市生活费用不断上涨。

normal.en: Keep the receipt to record the expense.
normal.cn: 保留收据以便记录这笔开支。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag on a distant dream.
abstract.cn: 想象遥远梦想上挂着价签。

abstract.en: Imagine trading time for a skill.
abstract.cn: 想象用时间换取一项技能。

abstract.en: Think of a receipt that proves a cost.
abstract.cn: 想象一张证明成本的收据。

examples.en: The company covers travel expenses for staff.
examples.cn: 公司为员工报销差旅费。

examples.en: They built the tower at the expense of the old park.
examples.cn: 他们以牺牲老公园为代价建起了高塔。

examples.en: The expense of heating the house shocked them.
examples.cn: 供暖费用让他们大吃一惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「expense」里有 ex（向外）+ pens（称量付钱）：向外付钱，就是「费用」。

root: 拉丁语 expensa（付出之钱）来自 expendere（称量后支付），核心义「为得到某物付出的钱」。

sensesIntro.en: Expense means the cost of something, money spent for work, or the sacrifice involved.
sensesIntro.cn: expense 意为某物的费用、为工作花掉的钱，或付出的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money laid down for something wanted.
core.cn: 核心意象：为想要的东西掏出的钱。

branches.en: The base sense is the cost of something.
branches.cn: 基础义是某物的费用。

branches.en: Costs are tied to work and can be repaid.
branches.cn: 费用与工作相关并可报销。

branches.en: A money cost becomes any sacrifice.
branches.cn: 金钱成本成为任何牺牲。

branches.en: General cost and work costs overlap.
branches.cn: 一般费用与公务开支相互重叠。

branches.en: Price and sacrifice share one idea of cost.
branches.cn: 价钱与牺牲共享同一个成本概念。

intro.en: Expense goes back to Latin expendere, to pay out.
intro.cn: expense 可追溯到拉丁语 expendere，意为付出钱。

latinIntro.en: Latin expensa and expendere supply the core forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expensa 与 expendere 提供核心词形。

definition_en: the gases around the earth, or the feeling of a place or situation
core_image: 一层薄薄的空气裹着地球
scene: 房间里的笑声忽然停了。 The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
sceneCN: 这里 atmosphere 是「气氛」（第 2 个义项：一个场合给人的整体感觉）；句意是屋里的气氛冷了下来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：大气的；有氛围的
副词：在气氛上
名词：大气干扰；气氛渲染

senses.title: Layer of gases
senses.definition: the mass of gases that surrounds the earth or another planet
senses.definitionCN: 包围地球或其他行星的气体层
senses.example: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳把热量困在大气层里。
senses.why: Atmosphere joins Greek atmos 'vapour' with sphaira 'sphere', so it literally names the ball of vapour wrapped around a planet.
senses.whyCN: atmosphere 把希腊语 atmos「气、蒸气」与 sphaira「球」合在一起，字面就是包在行星外面的一层气球。

senses.title: Feeling of a place
senses.definition: the overall feeling that a place or situation gives people
senses.definitionCN: 一个场合或情境给人的整体感受
senses.example: The atmosphere in the room turned cold.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里的气氛冷了下来。
senses.why: The air that surrounds and fills a room also surrounds a group of people, so the word shifts from the physical gas to the invisible mood that fills a space.
senses.whyCN: 充满房间、包围人的空气，同样包围着一群人；于是这个词从看得见的气体转成充满空间、看不见的情绪。

intro.en: Atmosphere was coined by joining two Greek words for vapour and sphere.
intro.cn: atmosphere 是把两个希腊词「气」与「球」拼起来造出的词。

items.en: atmos meant 'vapour or steam'.
items.cn: atmos 意为「气、蒸气」。

items.en: sphaira meant 'sphere or ball'.
items.cn: sphaira 意为「球体」。

items.en: Scientists coined atmosphere for the vapour around a planet.
items.cn: 科学家造出 atmosphere 一词，指包围行星的气层。

items.en: The word began to describe the mood of a place.
items.cn: 这个词开始用来描述一个场合的气氛。

items.en: Both the climate sense and the mood sense are standard.
items.cn: 大气义与气氛义都已成为标准用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sphere part; the near-meaning group names air and mood.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sphere 部分；近义组是表示空气与情绪的词。
